evidence: The static nesting arithmetic is correct and matches the frozen template: each gate is 600 s, their serial sum is 1200 < gate suite 1500; scored judges are 9000, 900 and 900 s, serial sum 10800 < scored suite 11100; 1500 + 11100 = 12600 < verifier 13200 (600 s remaining for other work). test.sh:207 uses --max-concurrent-agent 1; suite limits are at :213 and :224; each judge value is at judge.toml:4. task.toml:18/:21/:27 gives agent 7200 s, image build 600 s, verifier 13200 s. This confirms configuration, not workload sufficiency. The actual frozen workbook Quality Checks!D12 requires timeouts to be long enough as well as nested; its internal D12 says inner < outer and sum of judges < verifier. The relevant skill reference at quality-checks.md:50-51 also requires realistic cold-build and agent-build adequacy. Current policy qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:25-31 and qc/README.md:27 require hash-bound measured workload evidence. No runtime-evidence.json exists for this run. The raw index explicitly excludes configured judge runs and required measurement records. All 60 indexed artifact hashes and all frozen task/rule hashes matched when inspected; inspection.json preserves that verification. The raw browser logs give history wall_ms=5187.17013001442, post=1381.6342310011387, and runtime=116178.18322500587, each with scope "Continuous local reference browser proof; no LLM/provider/platform execution", criterion_verdicts_produced=false and a warning that browser time is not LLM judge overhead. The full-install binding establishes installation and health observations but gives no current configured judge elapsed time or realistic cold-build elapsed time. No current target-builder elapsed measurement is supplied. Historical candidate measurements are not transferred. The current functional judge has 80 binary outcomes collected through 22 protocols and a five-phase plan (functional/prompt.md:9,104-112), including successful controls, one restart, timed execution windows, independent browser contexts and bounded retries. Its prompt explicitly says the plan does not establish completion within the unchanged 9000-second limit (:112). A whole judge timeout can still lose observations (app_context.md:28). Liveness also remains unmeasured in the actual configured harness: test.sh:48-50/:136-138 permits two urlopen calls with timeout=2 and reads their bodies, then :116-121/:171-176 permits 120 iterations plus sleeps. 120*0.25=30 s is only sleep time; request waits can make the loop much longer (about 510 s under two full two-second request waits each iteration, excluding overhead). This cannot be assumed to fit the restart MCP outer 55 s (restart_mcp.py:11). The same code is in the frozen template, and integration.md:5 requires prompt health responses, so this review does not assert a measured conforming-app failure or authorize a shared harness change. It identifies an additional reason not to certify liveness from nominal constants alone. Only static arithmetic and raw scripted timing were reviewed; no configured judge/provider run, current cold build, or current builder run was performed. Required missing timing evidence blocks clearance despite the valid numerical nesting.
counterexample: Analytical challenge, not an observed runtime failure: a conforming alternative with accessible nested menus, native unsaved-work dialogs and a different editor layout can require more discovery and valid tool actions across all 80 outcomes than the scripted reference. If that configured functional judge exceeds 9000 s, correct app behavior loses an otherwise complete evaluation. Conversely, a broken app with a working basic Render/Save prerequisite but dead advanced callbacks or absent history can take shorter failure/fallback paths; a quick broken-app run or a quick scripted golden run cannot establish the successful full workload fits. No such app is claimed to have passed this timeout row or the configured verifier.
suggested_fix: Keep the current canonical budgets, preserve this evidence gap, and obtain an authorized exact-current full configured judge run with stage/judge elapsed times, liveness/restart/cleanup observations and raw hash-bound logs; also supply realistic cold-build and current builder timing evidence. Add the truthful timeouts_fit_the_work runtime record. If measurement identifies a shortfall, reduce redundant work without losing public coverage or apply a specifically justified authorized timeout change below five hours in a new candidate; do not infer adequacy from scripted timing or patch shared policy to produce a score.
